cases.title: The school closure

item.description: A screenshot of a district notice saying school is closed Friday for a water leak, forwarded in a group chat.

clues.A: A classmate forwarded it. Nobody knows who made it.
clues.B: The district website and official app say nothing about a closure.
clues.C: The logo looks right, but the date says Friday the 31st in a month with 30 days.
clues.D: It names no school building and no contact person.
clues.E: The classmate who made it admits he asked an AI app for “a school closure notice” as a joke.

cases.lesson: Screenshots are easy to fake. Go to the official source directly.

fib.wrong: Gotcha! Enjoy your Friday. At school.

cases.title: The flooded street

item.description: A flooded street, shared today with the caption “Our town right now!”

clues.A: A neighborhood page with lots of followers.
clues.B: A reverse image search finds the same photo in a news article from years ago, in another state.
clues.C: Nothing looks wrong. The water and reflections look natural.
clues.E: Asked which street, the page deletes the post.

cases.lesson: It’s a real photo with a false caption. A real photo can still tell a false story, so check when and where it was first posted.

fib.right: Fine. Real photo, wrong place and wrong year.
fib.wrong: Gotcha! A person took that photo. I just lied about where.

cases.title: The quitting streamer

item.description: Your favorite streamer, Skyla, seems to say she’s quitting forever.

clues.A: An account called SkylaLeaks, not her official one.
clues.B: Her official channels posted next week’s stream schedule.
clues.C: The voice sounds exactly like her.
clues.D: It skips her usual sign-off and never mentions her dog, who’s on every stream.
clues.E: Fans ask her directly. She posts “That’s not me!”

cases.lesson: Voices can be cloned. Check the person’s own official accounts.

fib.wrong: Gotcha! Cloned voice. Her real account said otherwise.

cases.title: The cell diagram

item.description: A plant cell diagram with very smooth, bright, perfect shapes.

clues.A: Your science teacher handed it out.
clues.B: The same diagram is in your textbook’s online resources.
clues.C: Every shape is perfectly smooth and brightly colored.
clues.D: The labels match your unit’s vocabulary words exactly.
clues.E: You ask. Your teacher shows you the textbook page it came from.
clues.F: A credit line at the bottom names the publisher’s illustrator.

cases.lesson: Smooth digital art isn’t automatically AI. Credits and sources tell you who made it.

fib.right: Bah. The credit line was right there.
fib.wrong: Ha! A human illustrator drew it. Smooth isn’t the same as AI.

cases.title: The glowing sneakers

item.description: A store sells glow-in-the-dark sneakers with three perfect product photos.

clues.A: A store you’ve never heard of that opened last month.
clues.B: The same photos appear on five other stores, all at different prices.
clues.C: In one photo, the laces go into the shoe and never come out.
clues.D: There are no customer photos, only perfect studio shots.
clues.E: You ask for a real photo. The store sends the same picture again.

cases.lesson: AI photos can sell products that don’t exist. Look for real customer photos.

fib.right: Rats. The laces were a mess.

cases.title: The bracelet fundraiser

item.description: A 7th grader raised money for the animal shelter by selling bracelets.

clues.A: Your local newspaper’s website, with a named reporter.
clues.B: The animal shelter thanked her on its own page.
clues.C: The photo is a bit blurry and her hand is cut off at the edge.
clues.D: It names her school and the shelter, and quotes her mom.
clues.E: You email the reporter. She replies with the day she interviewed them.

cases.lesson: Named people and places, confirmed by more than one source, are strong evidence.

fib.right: Hmph. The shelter backed her up.
fib.wrong: Ha! Real kid, real bracelets, real story.

cases.title: The essay sources

item.description: A classmate’s essay lists five sources, including The Secret Letters of the Mayflower by Dr. Helen Brooks.

clues.B: The library catalog and an online search find no such book.
clues.D: Sam can’t say what any of the books looked like or where he found them.
clues.E: Asked to bring one in, Sam says he’ll “look for it.”

cases.lesson: AI can invent sources that look real. Always check that a source exists.

fib.wrong: Gotcha! That book doesn’t exist. I made it up.

cases.title: The dancing robot

item.description: A robot dog dances smoothly to music at a technology fair.

clues.A: A local college’s engineering club posted it.
clues.B: The college news page has an article about the fair with photos of the same robot.
clues.C: The movement looks too smooth to be real.
clues.D: The club names the students who programmed the dance and the song they used.
clues.E: You ask how long it took. A student says three weeks and shares a clip of it falling over.

cases.lesson: Real technology can look unreal. Bloopers and behind-the-scenes clips are hard to fake.

fib.right: Fine. The blooper gave it away.
fib.wrong: Ha! Real robot. You thought the robot was the trick.

cases.title: The castle painting

item.description: Kai, an online friend, shares a detailed castle painting and says “drew this in an hour!”

clues.A: Kai, a friend you’ve never met in person.
clues.B: A search finds the same image on an AI art page, posted a week earlier.
clues.C: Some castle windows melt into each other.
clues.D: Kai has no sketches or older art to show.
clues.E: You ask which brush he used. Kai says “the normal one.”

cases.lesson: Ask to see the process. Real artists usually have sketches, layers or older work.

fib.wrong: Gotcha! Kai didn’t draw it. No person did.

cases.title: The storm warning

item.description: An urgent weather warning appears on your parent’s phone in capital letters.

clues.A: It arrived as an official emergency alert from the weather service.
clues.B: The local TV station and the city website post the same warning.
clues.C: The capital letters and urgent wording feel like a scam.
clues.D: It names your county and specific times.
clues.E: Your parent calls 311. They confirm the warning.
clues.F: It’s marked as an official emergency alert.

cases.lesson: Urgent doesn’t mean fake. Official channels that agree with each other can be trusted.

fib.wrong: Ha! It was real. Scary doesn’t mean fake.
